nodes.description: In Rpl3l knockout mouse hearts, ribosome occupancy at codons changes, and translation of contraction- and DCM-related transcripts is most affected. RPL3L-containing ribosomes collide less than RPL3-containing ones. A second knockout study found no change in translational efficiency, so the finding is contested and has not been tested in patient tissue.

nodes.description: Germline biallelic RPL3L variants, mostly missense in the conserved RPL3 domain, plus three frameshifts, the splice-donor allele c.1167+1G>A (exon 9 skipping) and one synonymous allele. In the 2026 meta-analysis of the 11 families known to that study, nine were compound heterozygous, and most patients combined a recurrent hotspot allele (Asp308Asn/Val in six families, Gly27Asp in three) with a private second allele. RPL3L is expressed only in cardiac and skeletal muscle and becomes the dominant RPL3-family protein in adult human left ventricular cardiomyocytes.

meta.association: Biallelic RPL3L variants are reported in CMD2D. The evidence rests on about 13 published families (16-17 patients), with segregation in several multiplex sibships, recurrent hotspot alleles across unrelated families, and functional data from one explanted heart and engineered AC16 cells. ClinGen rates the recessive pair Moderate under the broader dilated cardiomyopathy term (MONDO:0005021). The 2026 expert-panel "high evidence" category includes Moderate, so it does not imply Definitive or Strong.
